terms.grammar: adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis)
terms.comment: Named after Julius Caesar, who accepted a month named after himself (Suet. Jul. 76.1); before that it was Quīntīlis. Kalendae, Nōnae, Īdūs Jūliae: the 1st, 7th and 15th.

terms.grammar: adjective, with mēnsis; also a masculine noun (sc. mēnsis)
terms.comment: The fifth month, counting from March (quīntus; Varro, LL 6.34).

phrases.latin: Jūliō mēnse, quō maximē lītēs interquiēscunt
phrases.english: in July, when the lawcourts are at their quietest

phrases.latin: negōtium magnum est nāvigāre atque id mēnse Quīntīlī
phrases.english: sailing is hard work, and in July at that

quintilis.html: From quīntus. De Vaan 509, s.v. quīnque: the vowel of the ordinal was lengthened before the spirantized k (*kwīxto- > quīntus), and the long ī spread to quīnque. Traupman 78 marks Quīntīlis.
